task.name: RCL language workload matrix against CPython and rustc
task.description: Run matched text, sequence, UTF-8, JSON-shaped text and JSON compact-parse workloads through RCL, CPython and rustc where the provider contract is matched; record unsupported native domains separately.

metrics.description: Declared workload output match, represented as 1 or 0.
Average measured source preparation or build time. Python is py_compile preparation, not machine-code compilation.
Raw emitted artifact size; a footprint proxy, not total process memory.

notes: Uses RCL trim, lowercase, contains, choose and length builtins.
Uses RCL sequence construction and indexed reads against Python list sum and Rust array iteration.
The non-ASCII fixture is intentional: this measures actual UTF-8 byte encoding, not ASCII-only length.
This is a matched textual scan of JSON-shaped bytes. It is not JSON parser parity.
This is the first real RCL JSON parse-and-compact path; Rust is intentionally excluded because this repository does not provide a matching stdlib JSON parser reference.

capabilityGaps.reason: The current RCL Native VM has no declared file read/write capability in this benchmark contract.
The current RCL Native VM has no declared thread, async or parallel execution capability in this benchmark contract.

comparisonPolicy.reason: Each workload is compared on raw metrics only when every provider is PASS and shares the exact workload inputRoot. A workload loss is not hidden by an average.

notes: The matrix is a bounded language-runtime experiment, not a whole-language, ecosystem or commercial-product ranking.
Provider averages are descriptive only and never determine the dominance verdict.
Capability gaps are reported separately from executed workload comparisons and are not converted into fake provider passes.
